neighbours.label: names of Inner Asian peoples and places of China's western frontier (Tibetan, Uyghur, Mongol)
fire: Many Uighur families in Kashgar still trade at the Sunday market.
The monk Tenzin left his village in Tibet to study in a large monastery.
Kazakh and Kyrgyz herders graze their flocks in the high pastures of Xinjiang.
A Tibetan woman named Dolma sold butter tea beside the road to Shigatse.
The old Mongol banners of Inner Mongolia were reorganised after the war.
Pilgrims walked around the Jokhang temple in Lhasa spinning prayer wheels.
Uyghur musicians from Turpan played the dutar at the wedding.
The nomads of Qinghai, most of them Tibetans, moved their yaks to summer camps.
quiet: Many Berber families in Marrakesh still trade at the Sunday market.
The priest Mateo left his village in Peru to study in a large seminary.
Sami and Finnish herders graze their reindeer in the high pastures of Lapland.
A Quechua woman named Rosa sold corn beer beside the road to Cusco.
The old Scottish clans of the Highlands were reorganised after the war.
Pilgrims walked around the cathedral in Santiago carrying scallop shells.
Kurdish musicians from Erbil played the saz at the wedding.
The farmers of Guangdong, most of them Cantonese, moved their ducks to the rice fields.
